title: `one()` raises ValueError instead of my falsy custom `too_long` exception
spec:
This is the more-itertools library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 run_tests.py`.

`one` lets you pass `too_long` to raise instead of the default `ValueError`. That is ignored when the exception instance is falsy:

```python
import more_itertools as mi
class FalsyError(Exception):
    def __bool__(self):
        return False

mi.one([1, 2], too_long=FalsyError('too many'))
# expected: FalsyError('too many')
# actual:   ValueError: Expected exactly one item in iterable, but got 1, 2, and perhaps more.
```

Similar inputs are probably affected too; please fix the underlying problem rather than just this case.
acceptance: the reported example produces the expected output
the underlying problem is fixed, not just the reported input
